rationale: A hands-on probe confirms a live llms.txt at developer.box.com (HTTP 200, structured 'Box Dev Docs' index), and the evidence also shows agent-oriented markdown renditions of doc pages (e.g., /_llms/en/home.md, agent-configurator.md) that an agent can be pointed at directly. Missing for 10: independent or community corroboration of agents successfully using these docs, and evidence of a complete llms-full.txt-style bundle.

Box AI is documented to ask questions of, summarize, and extract metadata from files stored in Box. Box Hubs let users index curated content and get answers from Box AI, and the product site says users can co-create content with AI and summarize, extract, generate, and query content with permissions intact. Most of this evidence describes the developer API, though, rather than the in-product end-user experience. missing for 10: explicit evidence of proactive AI suggestions (not just answers or summaries), detailed docs on the in-app end-user Box AI experience, independent or hands-on corroboration.

The only direct evidence of background automation is a developer-site use case: when a PDF lands in an inbox folder, Box AI Extract automatically pulls fields into metadata (box-docs-12). It is unclear whether this is a configurable product feature or an example assembled from webhooks/events, which are developer building blocks and earn no credit here. missing for 10: documented user-configurable automation/workflow builder, trigger-action rules running autonomously, scheduling, details on how such automations are set up and managed, independent or hands-on corroboration.

Box ships a built-in AI, Box AI, that can ask questions about, summarize, extract metadata from, and generate content for files in Box (box-docs-9, box-docs-26). It also answers questions over curated Box Hubs (box-docs-13) and can run automated extraction when files land in a folder (box-docs-12). Its AI agents are configurable with selectable models (box-docs-18, box-docs-42), and box.com markets co-creating content with AI inside the product (box-docs-15). missing for 10: documentation of the in-app assistant UI rather than the API surface, evidence of delegating multi-step actions beyond summarize/extract/generate, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

Box can be driven entirely headlessly through its REST API with OAuth 2.0 bearer tokens, including a scriptable curl example. Box also documents a CLI for giving AI agents access to content and a way to mount Box folders into agent runtimes as a synced POSIX filesystem. Event feeds and webhooks support event-driven automation without a UI. missing for 10: explicit CI/CD pipeline guidance, documented non-interactive server-to-server auth for unattended runs (only OAuth and short-lived developer tokens are shown), detailed Box CLI docs, independent hands-on corroboration of CI usage.

Box ships Box AI agents, so it is fair to ask whether those agents can consume external MCP servers. However, the evidence only documents Box's own hosted MCP server at mcp.box.com, which is the server role and does not transfer to this client-side story. Nothing shows that Box AI or its agent configurator can register or call third-party MCP servers' tools.

Box is a SaaS content platform, not an agent, so the server axis applies. Its first-party docs describe a hosted official MCP server at https://mcp.box.com that lets AI agents search and use Box files over OAuth. A probe confirms the official remote MCP server documentation exists, and the developer homepage points agents to the Box MCP server. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that agents connect successfully, and detail on the tool set and connection steps.

Box documents first-party natural-language capabilities. The Box AI API lets you ask questions, summarize, extract and generate over content. The hosted MCP server at mcp.box.com lets AI agents search and use Box files, so a user can work with Box through an agent's natural-language interface. However, the evidence covers mainly querying and using content, not operating the product broadly (sharing, permissions, admin actions) through NL commands. missing for 10: documented NL control of core actions such as sharing, collaboration, uploads and folder management; a native in-product NL command interface; independent or hands-on corroboration.

Box's own developer site says agents can access Box content 'through the Box CLI or the Box MCP server,' which confirms an official, first-party CLI positioned for AI-agent workflows. That is the only mention in the evidence; nothing describes its commands, installation, auth flow or output formats. missing for 10: dedicated CLI documentation (install, commands, auth), evidence of agent-friendly features such as structured/JSON output, and independent or hands-on corroboration of CLI use.

Missing for 10: a machine-readable OpenAPI spec at the probed paths (all returned 404), and independent or hands-on corroboration of driving the product via the API.

Missing for 10: documented OAuth scopes or per-token permission restriction, agent-specific service accounts or app-level least-privilege configuration, token expiry/revocation controls, and independent corroboration.
